title: Plan: VRAM footprint or exact payload-reduction breakthrough audit

candidate_scope.candidate: recover VRAM without increasing host RAM or TTFT
questions: Can model/context/workspace/gate-cache memory be reduced enough to fit a top4096-equivalent exact up/down hotset?
What is the measured token-rate and TTFT penalty for each recovered GiB?
Does any placement change keep MemoryMax=16000000000 including page cache?
candidate_scope.reject_if: Recovered usable VRAM is below 13.8 GiB over the current top768-fit shape, or the gate-cache/TTFT penalty consumes the 1008 ms top4096 zero-overhead slack.

questions: Is there an exact/token-stable representation of hot up/down experts with at least 4.0x compression for top3072 or 5.33x for top4096?
Can decompression or direct compute from the representation fit inside the overhead slack?
Can fixed-text top1 equality be preserved?
candidate_scope.reject_if: Compression is generic entropy-only near the prior 1.04x result, or decompression/workspace violates VRAM/TTFT.

questions: Can selected fallback calls be removed without changing fixed-text top1?
How many fallback ms/calls/bytes are removed on the current profile?
Does the method generalize beyond the single France prompt or must it be marked prompt-specific?
candidate_scope.reject_if: It cannot prove token-level correctness before performance, or removes less than a top3072-equivalent fallback share without another saving mechanism.

must_include: Current accepted VRAM allocation and recoverable GiB by component
Required hotset payload and slack for top3072/top4096
Correctness gate and exact verifier command
required_artifact_before_code.promotion_rule: No runtime source edit until the hard-bound shows a plausible >10 tok/s route with at least 500 ms overhead slack, or an explicitly intermediate >4.4 tok/s SOTA candidate with accepted TTFT/correctness/RAM gates.

immediate_next_action: Collect a fresh accepted-path VRAM allocation snapshot and reconcile it with the top4096 payload requirement; then write the hard-bound decision before coding.
